-84.34950,33.90700.name: Reproductive Biology Associates
-84.34950,33.90700.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Daniel B. Shapiro, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

121.44000,31.20000.name: Syngenta Group China
121.44000,31.20000.desc: The Chinese arm of the state-owned Syngenta, and the vehicle through which seed sovereignty operates as industrial policy. China has moved from importing engineered soy and maize for feed to approving domestic cultivation, and the company positioned to supply it is one the state already owns. That is a different arrangement from four private corporations.

-0.13000,51.52200.name: Nuffield Council on Bioethics
-0.13000,51.52200.desc: A UK body producing detailed reports on genome editing, embryo research and farmed animals, with no statutory power at all. Its 2018 report concluding that heritable human genome editing could be ethically acceptable in some circumstances shifted the terms of a global argument, which is what a body like this does instead of regulating.

-77.10200,39.00000.name: All of Us Research Program
-77.10200,39.00000.desc: An NIH programme enrolling a million Americans, deliberately weighted toward groups underrepresented in genomic research. It is the largest attempt anywhere to correct the fact that reference genomes are overwhelmingly European, which is a scientific problem and a fairness problem at once: a risk score built on the wrong population is wrong for the person reading it.

13.34000,52.51400.name: Leibniz Institute for Zoo and Wildlife Research (Leibniz-IZW)
13.34000,52.51400.desc: The institute leading the consortium attempting to prevent the extinction of the northern white rhinoceros. Two females survive, a mother and daughter at a Kenyan conservancy, neither able to carry a pregnancy; living cells from twelve individuals are held in liquid nitrogen. In September 2023 the team achieved the first pregnancy in any rhinoceros after embryo transfer, using a southern white rhino embryo and surrogate — a technique routine in cattle and never before attempted in this family. The surrogate died of a clostridial infection resurfaced by heavy rains; the foetus was 70 days and 6.4 cm, and DNA analysis in January 2024 confirmed it came from the transfer. Twenty-one egg collections from the surviving daughter have produced 38 pure northern white rhino embryos; three transfers of those in late 2025 did not become lasting pregnancies. This is the honest version of what this facet promises: a decade of work, a proof of concept, and no calf yet.

121.47370,31.23040.name: Lilly Asia Ventures
121.47370,31.23040.state: Shanghai — with Hong Kong and Palo Alto
121.47370,31.23040.desc: A biomedical venture firm with roughly $4.5 billion under management, investing in biopharmaceuticals, medical technologies and diagnostics from seed to public stages across Asia and the United States. It began in 2008 as the corporate venture arm of a US pharmaceutical company and was spun out as an independent manager in 2011. That history is the entry. A corporate venture arm invests for strategic reasons as well as financial ones; an independent fund does not. This one was the first and became the second, while keeping the name — which is a useful reminder that the label on a fund describes its origin rather than its current obligations.
